raw_response:
I farm the way I always have: I start from last year, then I adjust a little if the price of inputs, water, or labor changes. I have 10.9 mu, and with wheat-maize as my main system, I will keep most of the land in that rotation because it is steady and I know what it can give me with well irrigation. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton still brings cash if I manage pests on time, but it takes more watching. With my years in the field, I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss hurts more. So I will keep wheat and maize fed a bit on the safe side, especially nitrogen, and I will still put some phosphorus underneath because our land responds to base fertilizer. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in as base plus a topdressing at jointing, and water about three times if the season is normal. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, sow quickly, mostly keep the straw and go with no-tillage to save time, then give two waters if rain is short. Cotton I will keep on the smaller area, use improved seed, plough it cleaner, feed it in splits, and spray more times because insects can turn it bad fast. I have family labor but not everybody stays home, so I will choose a plan that is not fancy, just solid, timely, and within what I can afford.
